title: Optimize walkthrough — Adaptive batching & cache roadmap with Lotus Dynamics
summary: Redwood AE/SE ran an Optimize console walkthrough focused on adaptive batching, prefix/KV prefetch strategies and three cost scenarios for Lotus Dynamics' chat workload. Discussed session affinity, TTLs, dedicated capacity, security pre-reqs (VPC, KMS, SOC2) and agreed on a short pilot and data handoffs.

Schedule a 1-hour pilot kickoff (Deep technical) week of 2026-03-29

Priya Nambiar: Produce simulation outputs (throughput/latency/cost) for 3 configs (hosted, dedicated, hybrid) (due 2026-03-24)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-19 15:30 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Marta Kim (Lotus - Head of ML), Ethan Zhao (Lotus - SRE), Lina Ortiz (Lotus - Product)
---
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, um i'll do a very quick intro, i'm jordan from redwood, i'm the AE on this account, priya is our systems eng and she will drive the optimize and console demo.
[00:08] Marta: hi thanks, excited to see the playbook, we've been focused on cost for our chat assistant after recent growth.
[00:12] Priya: great, i'll share my screen in a sec. quick qual — what's your current baseline qps and average prompt length? that helps set sims.
[00:20] Ethan: baseline is roughly 600 steady QPS with 1.6 second SLA for interactive sessions, token distribution center at 80 tokens per request, occasional spikes to 1.2k during promos.
[00:30] Lina: and we care most about unit cost — we have a target of 40% cheaper per session vs current managed provider, but latency can't exceed 1.8s p95.
[00:38] Jordan: perfect, that's helpful. objective for today: go through adaptive batching, prefix/KV prefetch TTLs, show console-sim cost scenarios, and agree next steps for a pilot.
[00:49] Priya: starting with a quick model of how batching interacts with KV cache. so redwood optimize will suggest an adaptive batch size curve based on live qps and seq len distribution — think of it as continuous batching that ramps batch size where latency budget allows.
[01:05] Marta: can you give a concrete example? like at 600 qps what does that look like?
[01:09] Priya: yes. for us demoing earlier — with 600 qps and 80 tokens average, the runtime chose an effective batch window of 12–18 requests for the short tail. that resulted in a 28% token-cost reduction due to higher batch efficiency plus KV reuse.
[01:24] Ethan: kv reuse — are you talking about prefix cache hit rate from sessionization or a lookahead prefetch?
[01:29] Priya: both. there are two levers: prefix (session-aware) caching where the KV cache stores prefix key states so repeated user sessions get high hit-rates; and lookahead prefetch where the console suggests prefetching likely next-token KV entries for predictable flows. in our sims prefetch increased hit-rate by ~12 points for flows with structured prompts.
[01:48] Lina: is prefetch expensive if wrong? like what if we prefetch and it's unused?
[01:53] Priya: good question — unused prefetch costs are essentially wasted token compute and memory. optimize's recommendation engine evaluates expected value: hit probability * saved tokens versus prefetch cost. we tune TTLs and lookahead breadth to keep expected negative cases low.
[02:07] [02:07] Jordan: quick interruption, small note on terms — sometimes fireflies transcribe KV as K-V or key V, so don't be alarmed if the transcript echoes that later.
[02:16] Marta: haha got it.
[02:18] Priya: moving to session affinity/routing; with your 1.2k promo spikes we recommend two-tier routing: (1) session-affinity for active users pinned to cached GPU workers to keep high hit rates, (2) fallback short-path to lower-cost quantized variants when capacity is constrained.
[02:35] Ethan: when you say quantized variants, are those lossy? how do we measure quality impact?
[02:40] Priya: usually small quality delta for many tasks. optimize includes an eval harness that runs A/B checks on a held-out prompt set — we produce BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics and business-key metrics you define (e.g., completion accuracy). in our sample the 4-bit quantized v2 had a 1.1% drop on intent accuracy but cut token compute by 36%.
[02:59] Lina: that's promising. but security is a blocker — we need SOC 2, VPC, KMS with HSM integration. what do you support?
[03:08] Jordan: we can do hosted but with customer-managed VPC for Private deployments; KMS/HSM integration is supported in our Private offering, and we have SOC 2 + ISO artifacts which i'll send. audit logs are available in the console with retention options.
[03:21] Marta: can you host a pilot on Dedicated reserved capacity so we see steady-state performance?
[03:26] Priya: yes, we can provision a small dedicated pool for the pilot — recommended for realistic latency/SLA testing. the console will let you change autoscale policies and set burst capacity.
[03:35] Jordan: i'll include a cost scenario for hosted vs dedicated vs hybrid — we typically show three scenarios: cost-min (aggressive batching + prefetch), latency-safe (tight latency SLO, less batching), balanced.
[03:47] Marta: walk me through those numbers for our workload.
[03:50] Priya: sure — quick numbers are illustrative: baseline provider cost per session = $0.045 (current). scenario A (cost-min) with long batching windows and prefetch: estimate $0.021 per session (~53% savings) but p95 latency climbs to 2.1s in peak. scenario B (balanced) with adaptive batching and restricted prefetch: $0.028 per session (~38% savings) p95 ~1.7s. scenario C (latency-safe) with small batch sizes and no prefetch: $0.038 (~15% savings) p95 ~1.5s. these were from our console sims using your token distribution.
[04:26] Ethan: the p95 2.1s is too high for us during promos. so scenario B seems nearest. how much of the savings depends on KV hit rate?
[04:35] Priya: roughly 40–60% of savings in scenario A came from KV/prefix cache reuse. batching contributed the rest. with your session patterns, if we get KV hit-rate above 45% you get heavy savings; if hit-rate drops below 20% batching still helps but ROI is lower.
[04:50] Lina: what's the operational complexity to maintain TTLs and prefetch rules? our team doesn't want a bespoke rule engine.
[04:56] Priya: we surface recommendations in the Optimize module. you get a suggested TTL and prefetch breadth per route, but you can keep the defaults and let Optimize auto-tune. console shows hit-rate time series, suggested changes, and one-click apply for TTL thresholds.
[05:12] Marta: can we see the console now?
[05:14] Priya: yep sharing screen — heading to Optimize > Scenarios. (screen audio) you'll see the traffic profile import, then three scenario cards with cost deltas.
[05:25] [05:25] Priya: noise in the transcript — sometimes vendor names get squashed, eg vertex vs vecter.
[05:29] Priya: here we toggle "adaptive batch sizing" to aggressive and you can see throughput improvements and the latency curve shifting right. notice the cost breakdown: compute tokens about 62% of cost, and NVMe memory ops + tail latency penalties are separate line items — that visibility is key.
[05:47] Marta: on the 'compute tokens' line — does that include prefetch waste?
[05:50] Priya: yes, prefetch compute is included. the sheet has a column for 'prefetch wasted fraction' so you can see expected cost of unused prefetch.
[05:59] Ethan: curious about warm KV priming for promos, can you do scheduled priming?
[06:03] Priya: yes, console has a priming job you can schedule before a campaign — it will load common session prefixes into the KV cache so hit-rates start high. we also support TTL overrides during promos.
[06:14] Lina: what's the memory footprint of KV for our scale? we worry about cost of large caches.
[06:20] Priya: estimate: for your typical 80-token sequence and expected unique prefixes, pilot pool with 4 x A100 equivalent will have KV memory footprint of ~200GB in aggregate; we give per-GPU recommendations and cost of NVMe spillover. that shows up in the console as 'cache infra cost'.
[06:37] [06:37] Jordan: quick digression — competitor question: anthro pic (anthropic) is known for adaptive batching; how is redwood different?
[06:43] Priya: two differences: first, our unified runtime ties batching to KV lifecycle: batch windows consider cache hit opportunities. second, Optimize auto-tunes batch sizing continuously by traffic and replays to balance token-cost and p95. competitors often have static batch heuristics.
[06:57] Marta: any gotchas around stateful session eviction when autoscaling?
[07:02] Priya: yes autoscaling can evict warm workers; we support session affinity to reduce churn and have transparent burst capacity that keeps a small warm pool during spikes. you can also configure sticky routing with a TTL-based affinity.
[07:15] Ethan: we'd like retention controls for audit — we can't keep full transcripts.
[07:19] Jordan: console supports configurable log retention for audit logs and we can anonymize or omit user text from logs for compliance.
[07:26] Marta: sounds good. can you summarize what you'd need from us for the pilot?
[07:30] Priya: three things: 1) traffic heatmap + token distribution CSV, 2) a small labeled prompt set for quality checks (50-100 items), 3) SRE contacts and any network constraints for VPC peering.
[07:41] Jordan: and we'll provide a cost model spreadsheet with the three scenarios, the pilot runbook and a SOC2/security packet.
[07:47] Lina: timeline?
[07:49] Jordan: if we get your heatmap by Friday (2026-03-21) we can stand up a pilot week of 2026-03-29, run two weeks of baseline vs config, and present results mid-April.
[08:00] Marta: ok let's do it.
[08:03] [08:03] Priya: switching back to a technical deep-dive; i'll show a small simulation live. this part is a bit noisy in the transcript because my screen share also had a terminal.
[08:12] Priya: running a 600 qps sim — note the console shows average batch size over time and KV hit heatmap. you can see at 600 qps the median batch size is 14, but the 95th batch grows to 42 during a promo.
[08:27] Ethan: can you toggle prefetch on/off quickly so we can spot delta?
[08:30] Priya: toggling now — prefetch off -> cost per session $0.034, p95 1.6s. prefetch on -> cost per session $0.028, p95 1.75s. delta reflects increased compute from prefetch but net token savings from hits.
[08:46] Marta: are these numbers deterministic? we need confidence intervals.
[08:50] Priya: sims produce 95% CI; we'll include that in the sheet. also we can run seed replays to test worst-case sequences.
[08:58] Jordan: a stakeholder question — what's needed for procurement? contracts, support SLAs, and pricing sheet?
[09:05] Marta: yes procurement will need pricing + SOC2 + SLA.
[09:08] Jordan: i'll attach pricing + standard SLA doc, and our legal can do a quick redline for enterprise terms.
[09:14] Lina: another question — can we roll in a data retention policy inside the pilot to test compliance?
[09:19] Priya: yes; we'll map retention per route and show audit logs that omit PII.
[09:24] Ethan: one more tech nuance — how does continuous batching affect cold-start for new models?
[09:29] Priya: cold models have longer kernel warm times; our runtime uses a small warm pool for new models and prefetching prioritized priming steps to reduce cold penalties. the console will show model warm time and recommend priming parameters.
[09:43] Marta: okay, really helpful. any risks to call out?
[09:47] Priya: main risk is over-aggressive prefetch leading to wasted compute if prompts are highly unpredictable; second risk is autoscale misconfiguration causing cache thrash. both are mitigated by conservative defaults and monitoring in Optimize.
[09:59] Jordan: recap and next steps: jordan send cost model + soc2 + pricing, priya run sim and provide logs, ethan provide heatmap and prompts. pilot kickoff week of 2026-03-29.
[10:12] Marta: agreed. thanks all.
---
Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings typical of automated transcription (KV => K-V, prefetched often transcribed as prefetch'd). Links shared: https://redwood.example.com/optimize/scenarios (demo sandbox), cost-model-template.xlsx (will be attached in follow-up).
